Tom — thanks for the clear list. Looping Marcus (SE) and Laura (pricing) so we can give both the technical and commercial view. Quick answers up front and a worksheet attached: Dedicated_Burst_Worksheet_Soojin_v1.xlsx.

High level:
- Throughput safety net: we guarantee a committed baseline throughput (tokens/sec or qps depending on your traffic shape) and define headroom as reserved capacity that we keep available for your pool. The guarantee is measured as availability of baseline capacity and p95 token latency below the agreed SLO during your sustained windows.
- Burst credit pools: typical sizing is 1.0–2.0x of baseline as a temporary credit pool. We can offer an elevated trial pool for onboarding.
- Cooldown: default policy uses a 30-minute sliding window for burst activity; sustained bursts longer than the window trigger throttling and/or surcharge depending on your chosen plan.
- Surge rates: charged per-minute over the pool; we usually offer slab pricing + an overage percentage (e.g., 25–40% premium on token unit price) rather than flat per-GPU minute to keep invoices predictable.
- Emergency DR carve-out: we can provide a separate DR burst pool on an exception basis with different cooldown (longer burst windows allowed) and a negotiated surcharge. This requires a line item in the commercial terms and an explicit ops runbook.

Action items:
- Marcus: can you confirm what headroom (p95 latency target and tokens/sec) we should model for the worksheet?
- Tom: please confirm your expected sustained baseline and the peak window duration in minutes/hours. That will let us populate the pricing worksheet and measure projected cost under different burst scenarios.

I attached the worksheet — it has three tabs: baseline sizing, burst pool scenarios, and cost projections for 12/24-month commits. Laura, feel free to propose discount schedules when you review.

Best,

Tom — quick technical clarifications to help populate the worksheet (copying the relevant snippet from Soojin's note):

"Throughput safety net: we guarantee a committed baseline throughput (tokens/sec or qps depending on your traffic shape) and define headroom as reserved capacity that we keep available for your pool."

A few specifics we'll use:
- Measurement: baseline is provisioned in vCPU/GPU-equivalents with an associated tokens/sec estimate; the p95 latency SLO is measured over 5-minute windows during your defined "sustained" periods. If your observed p95 exceeds the SLO and we aren't meeting throughput, we trigger remediation (auto-scale or priority routing) per the SLA.
- Headroom vs burst: headroom is short-term reserved overhead inside your Dedicated pool to absorb small spikes (recommended 15–30% of baseline). The burst credit pool is a consumable budget separate from headroom that can be exhausted; when it runs out, the cooldown policy begins.
- Commit sculpting (recommended): you can structure your reserved commit in tiers tied to predictable windowed demand. For example, a 1.0 commit for baseline, +0.5 commit for peak season, and then a burst add-on for unexpected surges. This reduces unit price for baseline while keeping flexibility for peaks.
- Cooldown / surge charging: our runtime evaluates bursts in 1-minute granularity. Default cooldown is 30 minutes of lookback for sustained activity; surcharge applies on a per-minute basis once burst credits are exhausted. Typical surcharge model is slabed: first 30 minutes at +25% unit price, next 60 minutes at +40%, sustained beyond that billed at negotiated spike rates.

If you want a carved-out DR pool (separate billing and relaxed cooldown), we'll treat it like a secondary capacity add-on with its own pricing and an ops-runbook. That avoids unexpected cross-impact on production pool.

I'll fill the worksheet with a sample "commit sculpting" scenario and run a cost projection for the month-over-month peak you provided in the RFP.

Tom — thanks, this is helpful. Based on the worksheet inputs Marcus will populate, here's a proposed commercial structure we can offer to match your Sep 15 timeline:

Summary of proposal (12-month term):
- Committed baseline: 100 GPU-equivalents (baseline) — unit economics at $X per GPU-hour (confidential in this thread).
- Discounting: 12-month commit = 12% standard discount; 12-month + 3x reserved commit sculpting (baseline + seasonal reserve) = 18% effective discount across committed units.
- Burst credit pool: onboarding credit pool = 1.5x baseline for the first 90 days (consumable). After onboarding, default burst pool = 0.5x baseline unless expanded as a paid add-on.
- Cooldown and surge pricing: default cooldown = 30-minute sliding window; surplus beyond burst pool billed at +30% over token unit price for first 60 min, +50% for next 120 min. Emergency DR carve-out: separate DR pool priced at +20% over baseline unit price with a 120-minute cooldown window and dedicated ops contact.
- One-time onboarding credit: $15k credit against first invoice if PO is received by Sep 15.

Next steps:
1) Marcus to finalize the populated worksheet by EOD Sep 8.
2) We'll attach a commercial term sheet and a redlined SLA (see attached).
3) Procurement to issue PO referencing deal ACME-2027-D1 by Sep 15 to lock these terms.

I attached the Proposed_Commercial_Termsheet_v3.pdf and a redwood-sla-draft.pdf for legal to review. If you need tweaks to the surcharge slabs or want to move to per-minute flat overage billing instead of percentage, we can model that too.

If you're comfortable, I can draft a short commercial exhibit that inserts the DR carve-out as a token line item so legal has something to review.
